audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 6, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal chronological, architectural, and witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for exodus chronology, temple measurements, skilled hidden labor, silence symbolism, conditional presence, cedar and gold extraction, cherubim imagery, sacred architecture, and seven-year construction.

verses.restored: In four hundred eightieth year after children of Israel came out from land of Egypt, in fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in month Ziv, second month, he began to build house of YHWH.
House King Solomon built for YHWH was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Porch before temple of house was twenty cubits long across width of house and ten cubits deep before house.
For house he made windows with recessed frames.
Against wall of house he built side chambers around walls of temple and inner sanctuary; he made chambers around.
Lowest chamber was five cubits wide, middle six, third seven; outside house he made ledges around so beams would not be inserted into walls of house.
When house was built, it was built of stone prepared at quarry; hammer, axe, or any iron tool was not heard in house while it was being built.
Entrance for middle side chamber was on right side of house. They went up by winding stairs to middle and from middle to third.
He built house and finished it, roofing house with beams and rows of cedar.
He built side chambers against all house, five cubits high, joined to house with cedar timber.
Word of YHWH came to Solomon, saying:
Concerning this house you are building: if you walk in my statutes, do my judgments, keep all my commands, and walk in them, I will establish with you my word spoken to David your father.
I will dwell among children of Israel and will not abandon my people Israel.
Solomon built house and finished it.
He built walls of house within with cedar boards, from floor of house to walls of ceiling. He covered inside with wood and floor with cypress planks.
He built twenty cubits at rear of house with cedar boards from floor to walls, making it inner sanctuary, most holy place.
House—that is, temple before inner sanctuary—was forty cubits.
Cedar within house was carved with gourds and open flowers; all was cedar, and no stone was seen.
He prepared inner sanctuary within house to set there ark of covenant of YHWH.
Inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty wide, and twenty high. He overlaid it with pure gold and overlaid cedar altar.
Solomon overlaid house within with pure gold and drew chains of gold across before inner sanctuary; he overlaid it with gold.
All house he overlaid with gold until all house was completed; also all altar by inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
Within inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olivewood, each ten cubits high.
One wing of cherub was five cubits and other wing five; ten cubits from tip of one wing to tip of other.
Second cherub was ten cubits; both cherubim had one measure and one form.
Height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so of second.
He placed cherubim within inner house. Wings stretched out: wing of one touched one wall, wing of other touched other wall, and their wings touched each other in middle of house.
He overlaid cherubim with gold.
Upon all walls of house around he carved figures of cherubim, palms, and open flowers, inside and outside.
Floor of house he overlaid with gold, inside and outside.
For entrance of inner sanctuary he made doors of olivewood; lintel and doorposts formed a fifth part.
On two olivewood doors he carved cherubim, palms, and open flowers, overlaid them with gold, and spread gold upon cherubim and palms.
Thus he made for entrance of temple doorposts of olivewood, a fourth part.
Two doors were cypress; two leaves of one door folded, and two leaves of other folded.
He carved cherubim, palms, and open flowers and overlaid them with gold fitted upon carving.
He built inner court with three rows of hewn stone and one row of cedar beams.
In fourth year foundation of house of YHWH was laid, in month Ziv.
In eleventh year, in month Bul, eighth month, house was finished in all its parts and according to all its plan. He built it seven years.

translation_notes: The 480-year chronology is a major historical and textual question and should not be presented as uncontested modern dating.
The building's silence is achieved by preparing stone elsewhere; it does not mean construction was effortless or quiet for quarry workers.
The central Divine word interrupts architectural detail to make presence conditional upon justice and covenant practice. The building itself cannot guarantee Divine residence.
Cedar, cypress, olivewood, stone, and gold connect worship to forests, mines, quarries, transport, craft knowledge, and ecological extraction.
The text attributes construction to Solomon while thousands of unnamed laborers, foreign specialists, artisans, planners, and carriers produced it.
Cherubim are ancient sacred throne/guardian imagery, not decorative proof for modern angel anatomy.
Gold saturation signals splendor and concentrated wealth. Sacred luxury should be read beside forced labor and palace extraction.
A temple can hold memory, prayer, and communal identity without containing or owning the Divine.
safety_note: Do not use the temple to sanctify exploitative construction, ecological destruction, wealth display, or claims that one institution possesses Divine presence. The chapter itself makes presence answer to faithful practice rather than architecture.
